text:
Alex: Quick design check — I want the synthetic generator to produce a 'folded spike' workload: tight micro-surges (~50–200ms bursts) separated by long idle tails (seconds to minutes), with explicit KV-cache warmup behavior so we can reproduce the kernel-selection + batch-pressure regression we saw yesterday. Any concerns?

Sam: Sounds good. Couple of asks: 1) we need per-client state so KV touch sequences are repeatable, 2) make the burst envelopes parametric (burst_duration, burst_qps, interburst_idle), 3) expose a `kernel_probe` mode that toggles the runtime's kernel selection bias for experiments.

Maria: Metrics to capture for apples-to-apples: p50/p95/p99, tail-latency histogram (log buckets), batch-size distribution over time, KV hit/miss rates, kernel-selection events (timestamp + reason), and queueing delay per-request. Also record the RNG seed used.

Jamie: Implementation idea — generator emits clients each with a Poisson think-time baseline, but bursts are scheduled by a higher-level "fold" pattern. Pseudoconfig: 
```json
{
  "clients": 200,
  "fold_pattern": {"folds_per_minute": 2, "burst_qps": 1200, "burst_ms": 150},
  "idle_tail_distribution": {"type": "pareto", "alpha": 1.8, "scale_ms": 1000},
  "kv_warmup": {"first_k_tokens": 64, "touch_pattern": "sequential"},
  "kernel_probe": true
}
```

Perf-bot: Baseline run (seed=42) on mainline: p95=78ms, p99=210ms, tail-spikes correlated with kernel-switch events at ~350k reqs/min, avg batch size=4.2, kv_hit=0.62.

Alex: Nice — we're trying to see if switching kernels under mixed short/long seq lengths creates spikes. How do we force the runtime to pick the "slow but memory-friendlier" kernel?

Sam: Runtime picks kernel primarily by (seq_len, batch_size, kv_cached_fraction). For experiments, `kernel_probe` will artificially bias selection by adding a +delta latency estimate to the default kernel so the selector prefers alternate kernels. We'll log both candidate scores.

Maria: For causal analysis, sample profiler stacks at 1Hz during bursts and tag samples with batch_size + selected_kernel. Also export the per-request `kernel_choice` attribute into traces so we can filter traces where choice != expected.

Jamie: Replay harness note — to get identical KV cache state between A/B runs: run a preheat phase with identical request stream and assert kv_hit fingerprint matches, then flip kernel flags while keeping seed and request timing identical. We'll add a `preheat_cycles` config.

Sam: Also: shape client think-time with a heavy tail to match production (Pareto alpha ~1.6–2.0). That produces occasional long idle gaps which let KV entries evict and create cold-KV conditions mid-burst. Add `eviction_window_ms` to generator to tune this.

Alex: Agree. Can we add a small script to export the exact kernel-selection decision matrix per-second so we can overlay with latency heatmaps?

Maria: Yep — I'll add a dashboard panel showing kernel_choice time-series, overlaid with p99. If we see aligned spikes, we can annotate the run and dig into kernel heuristics.

Perf-bot: Quick run idea: 3x A/B: (A) baseline kernel selector, (B) kernel_probe bias toward memory-friendly kernel, (C) forced no-kernel-switch (sticky kernel). All runs use same seed and preheat.

Jamie: One more practical: record the batch construction timeline (when requests enter queue vs when batch dispatched). That lets us separate queueing-induced latency from execution latency. We'll log `enqueue_ts` and `dispatch_ts` per request in debug runs.

Alex: Action items: Sam — add `fold_pattern`, `preheat_cycles`, `eviction_window_ms`, and `kernel_probe` flags to generator; include RNG seed in run artifacts. Maria — dashboard panels and profiler sampling hook. Jamie — replay harness preheat + exact timing replay. I'll queue the three A/B runs and post results here.

Sam: I'll start a branch tonight. Expect a first-pass generator binary in the morning.

Maria: SGTM. I'll stub dashboards and add alert if p99 exceeds baseline by +40%.

Perf-bot: Noted. Scheduled runs will be tagged `latency-fabric-test` and archived.

Alex: Thanks — let's keep the runs reproducible and save full kernel-selection logs. :thumbsup:
